steps.description:
Create a program that asks user to input the 4 points of a rectangle one by one. It will then call a function to find and return the horizontal length of the rectangle and display the returned result. The points are entered in clockwise order of the shape starting from top left corner:

You need to create a function that does the following: 1. Take in coordinates and calculate the horizontal length of the rectangle. 2. Return the result.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - length of a horizontal line is the difference in x-coordinates of the 2 points forming the line.

Test Input 1,6.5 9,6.5 9,1 1,1

-5,5 5,5 5,-10 -5,-10

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter point 1 (x,y): 1,6.5 Enter point 2 (x,y): 9,6.5 Enter point 3 (x,y): 9,1 Enter point 4 (x,y): 1,1 8.0

Example 2 Enter point 1 (x,y): -5,5 Enter point 2 (x,y): 5,5 Enter point 3 (x,y): 5,-10 Enter point 4 (x,y): -5,-10 10.0

Create a program that asks user to input the 4 points of a rectangle one by one. It will then call a function to find and return the vertical length of the rectangle and display the returned result. The points are entered in clockwise order of the shape starting from top left corner:

You need to create a function that does the following: 1. Take in coordinates and calculate the vertical length of the rectangle. 3. Return the result.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - length of a vertical line is the difference in y-coordinates of the 2 points forming the line.

Test Input 1,6.5 9,6.5 9,1 1,1

-5,5 5,5 5,-10 -5,-10

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below: Example 1 Enter point 1 (x,y): 1,6.5 Enter point 2 (x,y): 9,6.5 Enter point 3 (x,y): 9,1 Enter point 4 (x,y): 1,1 5.5

Example 2 Enter point 1 (x,y): -5,5 Enter point 2 (x,y): 5,5 Enter point 3 (x,y): 5,-10 Enter point 4 (x,y): -5,-10 15.0

A quadrilateral is a shape with 4 sides. Create a program that asks user to input the 4 points of a quadrilateral one by one. It will then call a function to check if it is a square and display the returned result. The points are entered in clockwise order of the shape starting from top left corner (below shows a rectangle):

You need to create the function that does the following: 1. Take in the coordinates of 4 points. 2 Determine if it is a square. 3. Return True if it is a square and False if otherwise.

For this question, practise storing each point as a list [x, y] to reduce the number of arguments being passed to the function. Assume that at least one side of the rectangle is horizontal so it will be not be rotated. You may add more functions as desired.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - A non-rotated square has 4 equal sides, 2 horizontal sides and 2 vertical sides. Do you need to check all of them?


Test Input 1,6 9,6 9,1 1,1

-5,5 5,5 5,-10 -5,-10

0,4 4,4 4,0 0,0

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below: Example 1 Enter point A (x,y): 1,6 Enter point B (x,y): 9,6 Enter point C (x,y): 9,1 Enter point D (x,y): 1,1 False

Example 2 Enter point A (x,y): -5,5 Enter point B (x,y): 5,5 Enter point C (x,y): 5,-10 Enter point D (x,y): -5,-10 False

Example 3 Enter point A (x,y): 0,4 Enter point B (x,y): 4,4 Enter point C (x,y): 4,0 Enter point D (x,y): 0,0 True

A quadrilateral is a shape with 4 sides. Create a program that asks user to input the 4 points of a quadrilateral one by one. It will then call a function to check if it is a square, parallelogram or otherwise and display the returned result. The points are entered in clockwise order of the shape starting from top left corner (below shows a rectangle):

You need to create the function that does the following: 1. Takes in the coordinates of 4 points 2 It will determine its shape and return "square", "parallelogram" or "other shape". Assume that at least one side of the quadrilateral will be on a horizontal or vertical line.

For this question, practise storing each point as a list [x, y] to reduce the number of arguments being passed to the function. Assume that at least one side of the quadrilateral is horizontal. You may add more functions as desired.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

1,6 4,6 4,3 1,3

-1.5,4.4 61,4.4 61,-5.6 -1.5,-5.6

3,71 9,71 4,-6 -2,-6

0,5 8,3 8,-2 0,0

1,1
2,1 4,0 0,0

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below: Example 1 (square) Enter point A (x,y): 1,6 Enter point B (x,y): 4,6 Enter point C (x,y): 4,3 Enter point D (x,y): 1,3 square

Example 2 (rectangle) Enter point A (x,y): -1.5,4.4 Enter point B (x,y): 61,4.4 Enter point C (x,y): 61,-5.6 Enter point D (x,y): -1.5,-5.6 other shape

Example 3 (parallelogram with horizontal sides) Enter point A (x,y): 3,71 Enter point B (x,y): 9,71 Enter point C (x,y): 4,-6 Enter point D (x,y): -2,-6 parallelogram

Example 4 (parallelogram with vertical sides) Enter point A (x,y): 0,5 Enter point B (x,y): 8,3 Enter point C (x,y): 8,-2 Enter point D (x,y): 0,0 parallelogram

Example 5 (trapezium) Enter point A (x,y): 1,1 Enter point B (x,y): 2,1 Enter point C (x,y): 4,0 Enter point D (x,y): 0,0 other shape
